subject: Maths
central_question: How can unit squares, decomposition, dissection and height-base relationships be used to derive and apply area formulae for triangles and polygons?
in_scope_units: Rectangles and squares, equal-area partitions and area measured by unit squares.
Area of a rectangle and comparison of rectangle areas.
Why perimeter cannot be used as a measure of area.
Areas of paths, crosspaths, tubes and composite rectangular regions.
Area of a triangle as one-half base times corresponding height.
Applications of the triangle formula, equal-area triangles, medians and triangles between parallel lines.
Reflection as a method for a shortest-path problem.
Area of any polygon by dividing it into triangles.
Area of a parallelogram derived by dissection into a rectangle.
Area of a rhombus from its diagonals.
Area of a trapezium from a rectangle-and-triangle decomposition and from two copies forming a parallelogram.
End-of-chapter mixed figures and area comparisons.
banned_topics: Surface area and volume of three-dimensional solids.
must_include_keywords: one-half height × sum of parallel sides

known_pitfalls.claim: Regions with equal perimeter always have equal area.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter shows that the same perimeter can enclose different areas, and a larger perimeter can even accompany a smaller area.

known_pitfalls.claim: Any side of a triangle can be paired with any altitude in the formula.
known_pitfalls.correction: The height must be perpendicular to the chosen base or its extension.

known_pitfalls.claim: The sloping side of a parallelogram is its height.
known_pitfalls.correction: Height is the perpendicular distance between the chosen base and the opposite parallel side.

known_pitfalls.claim: The area of a rhombus is the product of its diagonals.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is one-half the product of its diagonals.

known_pitfalls.claim: The area of a trapezium is height times the difference of the parallel sides.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is one-half the height times the sum of the two parallel sides.

recommended_example_progression: Use the opening 7 cm by 4 cm and 8 cm by 3 cm rectangles to compare 28 cm² and 24 cm².
Use the diagonal of the 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle to obtain two triangles of area 14 cm².
Use the triangle application that equates two base-height forms to find BY = 3.75 units.
Use the polygon Figure it Out Q1 with AC=22 cm and two perpendicular heights of 3 cm.
Use the parallelogram cut-and-rearrange derivation to obtain base×height.
Use the rhombus Figure it Out Q1 with diagonals 20 cm and 15 cm.
Use the two-copy trapezium derivation to obtain one-half h(a+b).
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Figure it Out sets follow the rectangle, triangle, polygon, parallelogram and rhombus-trapezium sections; the chapter closes with mixed applications, city-area exploration and the Summary.
